nodes.label: C1 - Short-term residual reversal (FF3-stripped)
nodes.author: Evan Daruwalla
nodes.rationale: FAIL, but the program's closest approach to PASS-HR: for the first time in 28 attempts BOTH gate legs cleared (19.08% CAGR / 57.7% DD vs E16's 16.76% / 65.9%). It fails because PASS-HR needs both windows and the secondary collapses to 2.92% CAGR / Sharpe 0.24 vs SPY's 11.98% / 0.74 - the effect is dead post-2014. Three compounding mechanisms: post-publication decay, survivorship (buying the biggest idiosyncratic losers among 39 KNOWN survivors is upper-bound-biased by construction, so the gate number is capped in meaning regardless), and severe cost fragility from weekly churn.

nodes.label: FF3-residual trailing-month ranking
nodes.rationale: Strip Fama-French 3-factor exposure from the formation return before ranking, so the reversal trades idiosyncratic dislocation rather than factor beta. It did exactly what BHLV promise - MORE return than E16's raw ranking AND drawdown pulled under the 60% ceiling - the rare case in this program where a literature refinement did what it says on the survivor tape.

nodes.label: Regime artifact plus survivorship stack (C1 failure mechanism)
nodes.rationale: All performance lives in 2000-2013 - crash-rebound decades where dip-buying survivors is maximally flattered - and vanishes in the modern regime (2.92% vs an equal-weight basket of the same names at 13.97%). A strategy whose edge requires 2000-2013-style volatility AND foreknowledge of survival is not deployable.
nodes.norm_label: regime artifact plus survivorship stack (c1 failure mechanism)

nodes.label: Weekly-churn cost fragility (C1)
nodes.rationale: 2,924 gate entries: the A->B rung costs -2.78 pp to the overnight gap (the Nagel close-anchoring cost), B->C costs -6.38 pp to weekly turnover at 5 bps, and 15 bps kills it outright (7.28% gate, NEGATIVE secondary).

nodes.label: C3 - Consolidated volatility-breakout kill-shot
nodes.author: Evan Daruwalla
nodes.rationale: FAIL - pre-registered as a kill-shot and it killed. 20d-high entry after a sub-median-vol squeeze, 10d-low or 40d exit, K=5, 29 ETFs, 5 bps: gate 3.62% CAGR / Sharpe 0.37, secondary 1.37% / 0.19, with 607 gate entries so it is well-powered rather than inconclusive. Closes the breakout/chart-pattern family, which now carries three consistent kills (E8, E11, C3).

nodes.label: Channel-low exit as a whipsaw tax
nodes.rationale: The instructive detail: the time-stop-only arm BEATS the channel exit (gate 6.19% vs 3.62%, -2.57 pp of damage) because the 10-session-low exit systematically sells whipsaws at their bottom. The 'exit discipline' that defines the chart pattern is what destroys it - measured honestly, retail TA's core loop 'cut losses at the recent low' is a tax. This validates the template's time-stop-baseline requirement.
nodes.norm_label: channel-low exit as a whipsaw tax

nodes.label: Time-stop-only baseline arm
nodes.rationale: Mandatory control arm in the experiment template: run the entry rule with a pure time stop so the exit rule's contribution is measurable rather than assumed. In C3 it was the arm that exposed the channel exit as negative-value.

nodes.label: C4 - Moreira-Muir vol-targeting sizing overlay
nodes.author: Evan Daruwalla
nodes.rationale: FAIL on the pre-registered bar, descriptive in value. Scaling E6 and E18 by w = min(1, 15%/sigma20d) improves BOTH directionally and clears no bar: every managed arm beats its unmanaged base on Sharpe in both windows, but the best (E18-managed, gate Sharpe 0.77) misses the 0.80 PASS-RA bar - and the bar was not relaxed post-hoc. Three costs of the improvement: absolute Sharpe still missed, return sacrificed (E6 secondary CAGR 14.81% -> 12.32%), and turnover triples-to-quintuples, making the gain cost-fragile.

nodes.label: Vol-targeting sizing rule w = min(1, 15%/sigma20d)
nodes.rationale: Continuous position sizing that sheds exposure where volatility clusters. It is a real drawdown-cutter on these sleeves (E6 gate DD 53.7% -> 25.1%, E18 43.6% -> 27.0% in the secondary), contra the strong Cederburg prior - but it cannot turn a sub-0.8-Sharpe overlay into a passing one.

nodes.label: C4 as the natural deployment shape (descriptive)
nodes.rationale: E18-managed is the best-behaved overlay variant the program has tested (Sharpe >= 0.77/0.94 both windows, DD <= 27% everywhere) and would be the natural deployment shape if the E6/E18 forward-paper candidate ever went live - but it earns no tier and changes no conclusion. Recorded as descriptive because there are too few independent stress episodes.
nodes.norm_label: c4 as the natural deployment shape (descriptive)

nodes.label: C6 - Even-week FOMC-cycle overlay
nodes.author: Evan Daruwalla
nodes.rationale: FAIL - the cleanest McLean-Pontiff decay exhibit the program has produced. The published signature replicates unmistakably in the gate (SPY +5.62 bps/day in even FOMC-cycle weeks vs -3.15 in odd) on independent code and a primary-source calendar, then INVERTS post-2014 (+3.69 even vs +6.60 odd). The tradeable overlay beats SPY in the gate but is nowhere near PASS-RA (0.34 vs 0.80), trails badly in the secondary, and its 1,585 toggles pay the toll ~48x/year, so 15 bps drives CAGR negative.

nodes.label: CMVJ even-week return signature
nodes.rationale: Equity returns concentrate in even weeks of the FOMC cycle. What a genuine-then-arbitraged anomaly looks like end to end: strong correctly-signed in-sample effect, full inversion out-of-sample after publication (2019 JF; visibly gone from ~2014), and an execution profile of hundreds of toggles that eats whatever marginal edge might remain.

nodes.label: data/fomc_announcement_dates.json - primary-source FOMC calendar
nodes.rationale: Compiled from federalreserve.gov 2026-07-14; using a primary-source calendar rather than a derived one is what makes the gate replication of CMVJ independent.

nodes.label: C7 - SVXY short-vol carry, VIX-TS gated
nodes.author: Evan Daruwalla
nodes.rationale: FAIL despite posting the highest full-window net CAGR the program ever produced (26.45%, 2012-2026). Two mutually-reinforcing grounds: risk-adjusted it LOSES to SPY (Sharpe 0.76 vs 0.82 at ~40% vol) and the bar required beating SPY on CAGR AND Sharpe; and the headline is an artifact of a dead instrument. The verdict is not kill-switch-sensitive - the no-kill-switch arm's 0.81 also loses to 0.82.
nodes.norm_label: c7 - svxy short-vol carry, vix-ts gated

nodes.label: Dead-instrument era split (SVXY -1x to -0.5x)
nodes.rationale: SVXY was -1x until 2018-02-27 and -0.5x after. Era-split, the -1x years did 47.33% / Sharpe 0.99 while the DEPLOYABLE-TODAY -0.5x era does 13.18% / 0.55 - SPY-like return at half SPY's risk-efficiency. The headline CAGR is therefore earned by an instrument that no longer exists.

nodes.label: Volmageddon dodge (effective-N = 1 tail evidence)
nodes.rationale: Contango flipped false at the 2018-02-02 close, so the gate exited at the 02-05 open and missed the -32% and -83% days - by one session, and after eating the -13.2% day. That is effective-N = 1 tail-dodging on the exact event the gate was designed around; XIV holders in the identical trade were terminated. An EOD overlay's protection against an overnight cascade is structurally a coin-flip on timing, which is why the prereg capped this at PROMISING.

nodes.label: C2 - dividend-initiation drift probe (closed for insufficient event flow)
nodes.rationale: BLOCKED-BY-DESIGN, no prereg written. Full dividend histories for the 39 survivors show only 3 first-ever in-window initiations in 26 years (MSFT 2003-02-19, ORCL 2009-04-06, CSCO 2011-03-29; AAPL-2012 is a resumption). n=3 cannot clear any pre-registerable event floor of 20-30, so the probe-first rule closed it before a runner was written. The initiation-drift literature lives in small/mid-cap universes the liquidity floor excludes.
nodes.norm_label: c2 - dividend-initiation drift probe (closed for insufficient event flow)

nodes.label: Volatility-risk-premium family survey (E18 -> X1 -> C4 -> C7)
nodes.rationale: Fully surveyed across four experiments: gate (E18), conditioning (X1), sizing (C4), harvest (C7). Conclusion - the VIX term-structure signal is a real regime CLASSIFIER whose one weak PASS-RA stands, but it is neither an alpha engine nor a safe carry harvester at EOD.
nodes.norm_label: volatility-risk-premium family survey (e18 -> x1 -> c4 -> c7)

nodes.label: M10-1 - Nagel Switch (VIX-gated reversal/trend)
nodes.author: Evan Daruwalla
nodes.rationale: The program's ONLY numerical PASS-HR (gate 17.87% / DD 59.95% / Sh 0.66; secondary 15.94% / 39.68% / 0.78) and explicitly capped as IN-SAMPLE-COMPOSED, survivor-flattered and razor-thin - recorded as 'PROMISING / forward paper REQUIRED', never a clean pass or a live claim. Simultaneously the best candidate the program has produced and a textbook case of why in-sample composition cannot be trusted.

nodes.label: Nagel Switch mechanism (VIX>20 -> reversal, VIX<=20 -> trend)
nodes.rationale: Trade C1 residual-reversal when VIX > 20 and E6 QQQ-trend when VIX <= 20. It escapes the proven fixed-weight impossibility because it routes on a CAUSAL variable rather than a fitted date - Nagel 2012 established that reversal alpha scales with VIX. The one honest defense against the snooping charge, and it removes only the worst form of it.
nodes.norm_label: nagel switch mechanism (vix>20 -> reversal, vix<=20 -> trend)

nodes.label: IN-SAMPLE-COMPOSED cap (why M10-1 is not a clean pass)
nodes.rationale: Seven compounding defects, any one of which caps the result: (1) composed AFTER 31 results on these exact two windows, choosing components because they were the survivors - severe multiple testing; (2) survivorship is concentrated exactly where the pass comes from, since the gate return is dominated by the reversal leg buying bottom-residual names in the 2000-02 and 2008 crashes among 39 KNOWN survivors while the delisted crashers are absent - this alone caps it at forward-paper-only; (3) gate DD passes by 0.05 pp (59.95% vs 60%); (4) threshold-fragile - VIX>18 drops gate CAGR to 14.83% and FAILS HR; (5) cost- and execution-fragile - c2c 22.82% -> next-open 17.87%, and 15 bps breaks it at 12.40%; (6) PASS-RA fails at Sharpe 0.66; (7) Nagel's 1998-2010 sample overlaps the gate window it is rewarded in.
nodes.norm_label: in-sample-composed cap (why m10-1 is not a clean pass)

nodes.label: What it would take to believe M10-1
nodes.rationale: Forward paper, live, at 5 bps, for a pre-committed horizon - the only evidence not contaminated by in-sample composition or survivorship. A clean test would also need a survivorship-free universe to expose the reversal leg's true crash losses, which the project's data cannot provide. Honest label: the first strategy to clear the return bar, on paper, under maximal favorable bias - promising enough to forward-test, nowhere near trustworthy enough to fund.
nodes.norm_label: what it would take to believe m10-1

nodes.label: Mark-to-market carry-forward bug fix (M10-1 runner)
nodes.rationale: The QQQ cache ends one session before some stocks, so a held QQQ was marked at 0 on the boundary date. Corrected to carry the last close; no look-ahead introduced. A data-vintage boundary defect of the same class the M12 audit later found in cache_fetch.

nodes.label: M10-2 - Gap-Amortized Stress IBS
nodes.author: Evan Daruwalla
nodes.rationale: FAIL, and the design fixed the overnight-gap problem which is EXACTLY how it fails. Holding 2x QQQ mean-reversion for 5 sessions after a stress-oversold trigger makes c2c (3.18%) and next-open (2.99%) nearly identical in the gate - the gap is neutralized - and with the gap removed the underlying trade is exposed as buying 2x QQQ into the 2000-02 and 2008 cascades and holding 5 days: a drawdown catastrophe at 83.3% DD, not hidden alpha. The strong secondary (28.95% / Sharpe 1.08) is a one-window bull-regime artifact of V-shaped snapbacks plus trend fallback.

nodes.label: Gap amortization via multi-day hold
nodes.rationale: Spreading the trade over 5 sessions amortizes the lost first night to near-irrelevance, where E2's 1-day hold made the gap roughly half the edge. This ISOLATES the reversion's true gap-free economics - which is the experiment's whole point, and they are terrible in the gate.

nodes.label: 2x leverage into index crashes is the killer (M10-1 contrast)
nodes.rationale: M10-1 passed HR with UNLEVERED CROSS-SECTIONAL reversal on survivors; M10-2 fails with 2x INDEX mean-reversion under the same VIX-stress conditioning. Same conditioning, opposite outcome - the difference is 2x leverage into index crashes (83% DD) versus 1x dispersed survivor names. That sharpens the read on M10-1: its pass is a cross-sectional-survivor effect, not a general stress-reversion edge.
nodes.norm_label: 2x leverage into index crashes is the killer (m10-1 contrast)

nodes.label: Synthetic 2x drag, QLD-calibrated
nodes.rationale: 2.00%/yr drag calibrated against QLD; overlap CAGR 31.11% real vs 30.97% synthetic. Faithful to E5/E6, leverage QQQ-only. No look-ahead: signal at close fills next open, and the c2c arm filling at the observed signal close is declared an explicit upper bound.

nodes.label: M11 - Algorithmic Chart-Pattern Detection
nodes.author: Evan Daruwalla
nodes.rationale: FAIL exactly as the a-priori brief predicted, and SIGNAL-DEAD rather than gap-dwelling or cost-gated. Rule-based (NOT LLM) causal detection of long-side reversal shapes - double-bottom and inverse-head-and-shoulders, entered on a fresh neckline break at close, filled next open - returns gate -0.14% CAGR / Sharpe 0.09 and secondary 1.67% / 0.19 on the 39 survivors, losing to SPY and to equal-weight buy-hold of its own universe. The 9th equity family and the first to trade SHAPE rather than a NUMBER.

nodes.label: SIGNAL-DEAD failure category
nodes.rationale: Rung A (c2c) ~= Rung B (next-open) ~= 0% in the gate: unlike the IBS family which lost over half its edge A->B to the overnight gap, or E13 which was cost-gated, the long-reversal shape has NO GROSS EDGE TO LOSE. Even frictionless the gate is +0.61%. That makes this the cleanest kind of negative - the E14 category - because no execution or cost improvement could rescue it.

nodes.label: Short-side diagnostic: survivorship inverts the documented pattern edge
nodes.rationale: Never traded, reported as a diagnostic: after a LONG-reversal completion mean forward-20 return is +0.82%, BELOW the unconditional +1.15%; after a BEARISH completion it is +1.70%, ABOVE unconditional. Opposite to what retail TA teaches and opposite in sign to Savin-Weller-Zvingelis. The reason is structural - survivorship removed exactly the names whose head-and-shoulders correctly foretold a decline, so on a survivor mega-cap set a top pattern is just a pause in a name that by construction kept rising. Survivor bias does not merely inflate long dip-buying; it ERASES the one pattern edge the literature documents.
nodes.norm_label: short-side diagnostic: survivorship inverts the documented pattern edge

nodes.label: Causal close-based pivot detector (w=5, LMW convention)
nodes.rationale: One consolidated spec with parameters pinned a priori and never tuned post-result, using close-based causal pivots because LMW's two-sided kernel smoother is non-causal and therefore look-ahead for trading. Oversubscription drops (738 gate signals down to 314 entries) are the K=3 cap on clustered signals - disclosed, not silent; a larger K would dilute toward the EW-39 benchmark which is itself -0.47%.
nodes.norm_label: causal close-based pivot detector (w=5, lmw convention)

nodes.label: X3 - Reg SHO daily short-volume drift
nodes.author: Evan Daruwalla
nodes.rationale: FAIL. The long-only lowest-SVR leg posts gate 13.00% / Sharpe 0.75 against SPY's 14.80% / 0.91 - losing on BOTH - and the existence spread (low-SVR minus high-SVR) is +1.24% at Sharpe 0.16, i.e. the two baskets at 14.74% vs 12.05% are statistically indistinguishable. Whatever gross lift the long leg shows is a least-shorted-large-cap beta tilt, not a short-volume edge. Costs finish it: 15 bps takes the gate to 1.83% and the secondary negative.
nodes.norm_label: x3 - reg sho daily short-volume drift

nodes.label: Short VOLUME is market-maker hedging noise, not informed shorting
nodes.rationale: The near-zero spread is the whole story: a real informed-shorting signal would separate the low- and high-SVR baskets, but they sit within ~2.7 pp/yr at Sharpe 0.16. Executed short volume is dominated by wholesaler and market-maker hedge prints - SVR sits 25-52% for EVERYONE - so ranking on it sorts microstructure rather than information. This confirms the contamination flagged at ingest.
nodes.norm_label: short volume is market-maker hedging noise, not informed shorting

nodes.label: X2/X3 contrast - short INTEREST vs short VOLUME
nodes.rationale: Same family, same universe, same machinery: short INTEREST (settlement positions) carries a real, correctly-signed +18.39% short-side anomaly that is nonetheless untradeable at this capital; short VOLUME (executed flow) carries essentially no cross-sectional signal at all. Both route to FAIL for different and now-documented reasons - which is the payload.
nodes.norm_label: x2/x3 contrast - short interest vs short volume

nodes.label: X6 - Crypto BTC/ETH time-series trend (paper-first)
nodes.author: Evan Daruwalla
nodes.rationale: FAIL, PROMISING-capped. A BTC/ETH dual-MA sleeve (SMA20 > SMA100, long-or-flat, next-bar, 25 bps/side) crushes buy-and-hold in the bear-heavy 2018-22 gate - 29.6% CAGR vs HODL 4.3%, Sharpe 0.76 vs 0.43, drawdown cut 82% -> 61% - then loses to HODL's raw Sharpe in the 2023+ bull (0.76 vs 1.01), failing the beat-HODL-in-BOTH-windows bar. The program's first crypto experiment; stepping outside equities did not escape the structural finding.

nodes.label: The crypto fee wall is real for high-frequency, not for slow trend
nodes.rationale: The feasibility brief's governing worry - 25 bps/side, 5x equity - assumed a taker-heavy cadence. A 20/100 MA overlay toggles ~6x/yr, so 33 toggles over 5 years makes fees a rounding error: gate CAGR 30.26% at 10 bps, 29.61% at 25 bps, 28.55% at 50 bps. An a-priori cost objection empirically refuted for THIS strategy shape.
nodes.norm_label: the crypto fee wall is real for high-frequency, not for slow trend

nodes.label: Trend as drawdown control, not return enhancement (new asset class)
nodes.rationale: Crypto reproduces the equity E6 conclusion precisely: MA trend triples HODL's return and cuts an 82% drawdown to 61% across the 2018/2022 bears, then gives the edge back in the 2023-25 bull where simply holding wins on Sharpe because you sit flat through pullbacks that immediately recover. The program's structural conclusion generalizes beyond equities.
nodes.norm_label: trend as drawdown control, not return enhancement (new asset class)

nodes.label: Survivor majors - the sleeve-vs-HODL delta is the honest read
nodes.rationale: BTC and ETH are the two survivor majors, so absolute CAGR is upper-bound-biased just as the 39-name equity universe is. The survivorship-robust quantity is the delta against HODL, and it says 'better in bears, worse in bulls' - a timing overlay, not alpha. Live-money crypto stays Evan-gated regardless because custody is the deciding, undiversifiable risk.
nodes.norm_label: survivor majors - the sleeve-vs-hodl delta is the honest read

nodes.label: Research Brief - Algorithmic Chart-Pattern Detection (M11.1)
nodes.author: Evan Daruwalla
nodes.rationale: NOT a results doc and carries no D1 verdict - it is the stage-before-prereg survey written BEFORE M11 ran, stating an honest a-priori FAIL prior with the evidence explicitly labelled MIXED. Its recommendation was to run M11 as an honest kill-shot rather than a hopeful engine, closing the last untested mechanism gap. Every one of its predictions was confirmed by M11.

nodes.label: Informative != profitable
nodes.rationale: LMW's own caveat, and the brief's first load-bearing fact: patterns carry real but modest incremental STATISTICAL information - a claim about conditional return distributions - which is not the same as a cost-surviving trading rule. Patterns optimal for detecting statistical anomalies need not be optimal for trading profits.

nodes.label: The best-evidenced pattern sits on the side this project cannot trade
nodes.rationale: The tradeable evidence concentrates on the SIDE (short/hedged) and STRUCTURE (large diversified books) the mandate structurally forbids, while the deployable LONG-only side has materially weaker documented support. This is the X2 lesson repeated at the pattern layer: the strongest documented edge is behind the no-fractional-shorting wall at $100-1,000.
nodes.norm_label: the best-evidenced pattern sits on the side this project cannot trade

nodes.label: LMW kernel smoother look-ahead trap
nodes.rationale: LMW's two-sided kernel regression uses future prices at every smoothed point - fine for their statistical study, look-ahead for trading. A deployable detector must use a causal smoother or confirm only after the neckline break. Pattern presence is also subjective, so the detector's tolerance parameters are a snooping surface that must be pinned a priori.

nodes.label: Multi-pattern search as the snooping surface
nodes.rationale: Trying many patterns and parameters IS the failure mode STW and Bajgrowicz-Scaillet document, so the prereg must pin ONE consolidated spec or snoop-adjust explicitly. This is why design option 1 (single spec) was recommended over option 2 (broad scanner under FDR - maximal snooping surface, heaviest build, near-certain null) and option 3 (continuation patterns - already killed three times).
nodes.norm_label: multi-pattern search as the snooping surface

nodes.label: M3 Forward Paper - setup notes (infrastructure, no verdict)
nodes.author: Evan Daruwalla
nodes.rationale: Explicitly NOT an experiment write-up and issues no D1 verdict. Documents the forward-paper build for PRD M3 tasks 14-17, a dated design adaptation away from the stale e1_control/e1_llm_veto spec, two operational findings from the first dry run, and what stays blocked on Evan. M3 is the only untested lever that could validate M10-1.
nodes.norm_label: m3 forward paper - setup notes (infrastructure, no verdict)

nodes.label: Adaptation from the stale M3 spec (dated decision 2026-07-15)
nodes.rationale: PRD tasks 14/18 were written in the M0 era and name e1_control and e1_llm_veto sleeves; E1 FAILED and was shelved in M2b, so those sleeves no longer correspond to anything worth forward-testing. Superseded by the three D1 tier-clearing (or in-sample-clearing) survivors. The LLM-overlay design at PRD M9 task 51 is untouched and remains a separate, later, forward-only treatment arm.
nodes.norm_label: adaptation from the stale m3 spec (dated decision 2026-07-15)

nodes.label: e6_1x sleeve - QQQ 1x, invested iff QQQ > 200-DMA
nodes.rationale: Simplest sleeve - one instrument, a handful of switches per year - and recommended as the first live mirror precisely because the lowest plumbing-bug risk protects the evidence trail. A beta-timing overlay: it decides WHEN to hold QQQ, not WHAT to hold, so it generates no selection alpha.
nodes.norm_label: e6_1x sleeve - qqq 1x, invested iff qqq > 200-dma

nodes.label: e18_vixts sleeve - QQQ 1x, invested iff VIX/VIX3M < 1
nodes.rationale: E18 arm (a), prereg f32b008; the program's first and only PASS-RA, and a weak one - largely 'dodged 2008'. When VIX3M's feed lags, decide_e18_vixts returns None with a stated reason and the sleeve holds its position: safe inertial degradation, never a guessed trade.
nodes.norm_label: e18_vixts sleeve - qqq 1x, invested iff vix/vix3m < 1

nodes.label: m10_1_nagel sleeve - weekly VIX-gated reversal/trend switch
nodes.rationale: VIX>20 routes to a bottom-K=4 FF3-residual reversal basket on the 39-survivor universe; VIX<=20 routes to E6 trend. The program's first PASS-HR and IN-SAMPLE-COMPOSED - this is the one M3 exists to actually validate. It is also the only one of the three sleeves that is a genuine cross-sectional selection strategy, and it is momentum's mirror image.
nodes.norm_label: m10_1_nagel sleeve - weekly vix-gated reversal/trend switch

nodes.label: 3-account model - one Alpaca paper account per sleeve
nodes.rationale: Three separate $1,000 paper accounts, one per sleeve - better than the original single-mirror plan because order flow is fully isolated, which retires the SWING_ALPACA_SLEEVE selector. Two real format issues were caught and fixed in CODE rather than by touching the keys: the base URL ending in /v2 would have doubled paths to /v2/v2/..., and Alpaca rejects notional+limit orders so buys became market-notional DAY. Verified read-only with no orders placed: all 3 accounts 200 OK / ACTIVE / $1,000 cash, distinct account numbers.
nodes.norm_label: 3-account model - one alpaca paper account per sleeve

nodes.label: realize_pending same-session fill bug (found by the first dry run)
nodes.rationale: Running the script twice on the same still-latest session filled the pending order against its OWN signal day's open - one day too early, and non-idempotent on re-runs. Fixed by requiring today > pending_signal_date (strictly later session) before filling; verified with two consecutive same-day runs both reporting filled-today: False. The buggy run's test fills were deleted before any real use.
nodes.norm_label: realize_pending same-session fill bug (found by the first dry run)

nodes.label: Two operational data-feed findings (disclosed, not bugs)
nodes.rationale: (1) Yahoo's same-day bar can stay incomplete for hours after the close, and prices.fetch correctly drops any row with a NaN OHLC, so a late-night run can silently fall back a session - hence schedule the nightly run late evening (~8-9pm ET), not right after 4pm ET. (2) ^VIX3M's feed lags ^VIX's by at least one session, which is why the e18 decision must degrade inertially rather than guess.
nodes.norm_label: two operational data-feed findings (disclosed, not bugs)

nodes.label: BLOCKED-ON-EVAN items and the deliberate no-scheduling stance
nodes.rationale: Accounts and keys are DONE; what remains is authorizing the first real --execute run (no paper orders placed yet), the still-unverified after-hours DAY-order queuing assumption that the first fill_divergence row will settle, and the Task Scheduler entry. Scheduling was deliberately NOT created: an unattended process submitting real order flow to a live brokerage API needs Evan to set it up explicitly. 'Set up + keys' is not 'start trading'.
nodes.norm_label: blocked-on-evan items and the deliberate no-scheduling stance

nodes.label: X7 - HYG:IEF credit-appetite regime gate
nodes.author: Evan Daruwalla
nodes.rationale: FAIL (PROMISING-capped window, and it did not reach PROMISING) but the most interesting gate result since E18: the FIRST gate in the program to beat the plain 200-DMA in a window. Long QQQ when the HYG:IEF ratio exceeds its 200-day SMA, else cash - the free credit-spread proxy E18's HY-OAS arm could not test. Attempt 35, within the E18 regime-gate lineage.

nodes.label: Crisis specialist that self-destructs in bull markets
nodes.rationale: In the GFC gate credit genuinely led equities and de-risked earlier, cutting drawdown to 12.9% vs the 200-DMA's 20.3% at Sharpe 0.98 vs 0.61. In 2014+ the ratio dips on every spread wobble (energy 2015-16, Q4-2018, COVID, 2022) that the 200-DMA rode through, so the gate sells low and buys back higher: 3.81% CAGR on a 47.6% drawdown, WORSE than simply holding QQQ. 221 switches vs the 200-DMA's 172 - it is the noisier signal, and the noise is fatal in a trending bull. A 50-day ratio-MA is even better in the gate and still fails the secondary, so the pattern is not a window artifact.
nodes.norm_label: crisis specialist that self-destructs in bull markets

nodes.label: X7's FAIL is clean in both directions (market-wide ETF signal)
nodes.rationale: Unlike the survivor-universe experiments, X7 uses a market-wide ETF signal so it carries no survivorship bias - the result is interpretable in BOTH directions and a pass would have been meaningful (though forward-paper-routed by the modified window). The HYG-start-2007 window misses 2000-02 and the 200-DMA warmup keeps the gate in cash through ~2008-01, which handicaps its early gate return - so beating the incumbent anyway makes the result conservative. Prices are dividend-UNADJUSTED, correct for a regime signal and never traded as a return series.
nodes.norm_label: x7's fail is clean in both directions (market-wide etf signal)

nodes.label: Cross-project comparison - Swing (3 sleeves) vs Trading (momentum, 27 sleeves)
nodes.author: Evan Daruwalla
nodes.rationale: Not an experiment - no verdict, no tally change. Trading was inspected READ-ONLY per the project hard rule. The two paper programs sit at opposite ends of one spectrum and are complements: near-orthogonal signals (momentum vs reversal, broad vs QQQ, monthly vs daily) run on separate broker accounts in the same era, forming a natural experiment across concentration, horizon and capital scale at once.
nodes.norm_label: cross-project comparison - swing (3 sleeves) vs trading (momentum, 27 sleeves)

nodes.label: Trading is the control for Swing's negative result
nodes.rationale: momentum_v2 does the 'right' thing - top-50 equal-weight across ~5,200 names - and validated (IS +21.0%/yr, OOS +26.5%/yr, OOS Sharpe 0.87). Read together with Swing's 0-for-35, the claimed conclusion was that the problem is not that factors fail but that retail constraints (K=1-4, $1K, liquidity floor) forbid the breadth the premium requires. M12 later OVERTURNED the breadth half of this claim: turnover, not breadth, was the binding constraint.
nodes.norm_label: trading is the control for swing's negative result

nodes.label: Validation asymmetry - research instrument vs track record
nodes.rationale: Trading harvests a known robust premium with a real forward track record; Swing's three sleeves are hypotheses the program itself distrusts - m10_1_nagel IN-SAMPLE-COMPOSED, e18_vixts a WEAK PASS-RA, e6_1x market-dependent (works in 3 of 5 non-US regimes). Skeptical in both directions: momentum_v2's in-sample mean-yearly Sharpe is only 0.23 and its headline 0.87 OOS Sharpe is a 2024-26 bull with no momentum crash in the window - the same one-window flattery Swing kills experiments for.
nodes.norm_label: validation asymmetry - research instrument vs track record

nodes.label: Trading repo - momentum_v2 (12-1 cross-sectional momentum, locked 2026-05-26)
nodes.rationale: Read READ-ONLY from this project; never modified. Top-50 equal-weight at 2% NAV each over ~5,200 US names, monthly rebalance, $100K/sleeve, 5 bp half-spread. The literal opposite sign and horizon to m10_1_nagel's bottom-K residual reversal, which is why running both is genuinely diversifying rather than redundant.
nodes.norm_label: trading repo - momentum_v2 (12-1 cross-sectional momentum, locked 2026-05-26)

nodes.label: X8 - non-equity trend sleeve (decorrelation candidate)
nodes.author: Evan Daruwalla
nodes.rationale: FAIL both arms, attempt 36, deploy nothing. The E6 rule verbatim (long iff close > SMA200, next open, 1 bp/side, K=1, $1,000) applied to GLD and TLT. The useful part is HOW they failed: decorrelation was never the hard problem - both arms cleared the <=0.30 correlation bar by a mile (GLD +0.089, TLT -0.191) and neither could beat simply HOLDING the same asset. Finding an uncorrelated asset is easy; finding one where this program's single surviving rule adds value is not.

nodes.label: Arm (a) GLD - a genuine near-miss, 3 of 4 criteria
nodes.rationale: Correlation, positive CAGR and drawdown all PASS; criterion 4 (Sharpe > buy-hold in both windows) splits the windows - trend beats buy-hold in GATE (0.73 vs 0.65) and loses in SEC (0.52 vs 0.65). The sixth appearance of the program's signature death. What the gate DID do is cut GFC-era drawdown by a third (37.8% -> 24.5%), confirming E6's lesson in a third asset class.
nodes.norm_label: arm (a) gld - a genuine near-miss, 3 of 4 criteria

nodes.label: Arm (b) TLT - declared dividend-UNADJUSTED bias
nodes.rationale: Dividend-unadjusted prices materially understate a coupon-bearing asset, so TLT's real total return was meaningfully better than the -0.45%/-0.74% shown - the convention that is correct for the rest of the project is WRONG for this instrument. Recorded as a limitation rather than quietly dropped. Even so the arm fails criterion 4 independently of the dividend issue, because that comparison is internally consistent (both sides unadjusted). A total-return data path is a real gap in the project's data layer, not just this experiment's.

nodes.label: The uncomfortable observation - plain buy-and-hold GLD decorrelates better
nodes.rationale: Same low correlation, higher Sharpe in BOTH windows (0.65/0.65 vs 0.73/0.52) than the trend-gated version. But buy-and-hold is an allocation, not a swing strategy, and sits outside the program's days-to-weeks scope - saying so is the accurate reading of the numbers, not a recommendation to buy gold.
nodes.norm_label: the uncomfortable observation - plain buy-and-hold gld decorrelates better

nodes.label: M12 - constraint-relaxation factorial (horizon binds, breadth does not)
nodes.author: Evan Daruwalla
nodes.rationale: Attempt 38, DIAGNOSTIC - issues no PASS/FAIL and no cell becomes a sleeve, because picking the best of four and deploying it is in-sample composition, the already-documented M10-1 mistake. A 2x2 over hold length (10 vs 63 sessions) and breadth (K=3 vs K=20) on 142 large-caps. Its job was to ATTRIBUTE the failure, and it did.
nodes.norm_label: m12 - constraint-relaxation factorial (horizon binds, breadth does not)

nodes.label: Horizon was the binding constraint - and the mechanism is turnover
nodes.rationale: Lengthening the hold 10 -> 63 sessions adds +7.98 pp GATE / +1.87 pp SEC at 5 bps and +12.29 / +7.05 pp at 15 bps. The effect GROWS with cost, which is the mechanical signature of a turnover problem rather than a signal one - turnover falls 50.2x to 7.7x per year. Same lesson X9 delivered by inference ('the signal is smaller than the toll'), now confirmed by direct experiment.
nodes.norm_label: horizon was the binding constraint - and the mechanism is turnover

nodes.label: Breadth does not bind - M12 overturns the program's stated explanation
nodes.rationale: The cross-project comparison had asserted that retail constraints forbid the breadth the premium requires. M12 says that was wrong: K=3 -> K=20 helps negligibly in GATE (+1.28 pp) and HURTS materially in SEC (-10.23 pp), with a negative interaction (-8.01 / -3.34 pp) so breadth actively destroys the horizon gain. At K=20 of 142 you hold 14% of the universe and converge toward the equal-weight benchmark - visible as cell 3's SEC +16.43% drifting toward EW's +12.11% while cell 2 stays at +28.53%. Caveat: 142 names is a 14% sort, not momentum_v2's 1% sort, so this tests the DIRECTION of the concentration effect, not its magnitude.
nodes.norm_label: breadth does not bind - m12 overturns the program's stated explanation

nodes.label: Mixed-vintage cache corruption (published SEC numbers were WRONG)
nodes.rationale: A cold audit found cache_fetch had NO freshness check and returned price files of mixed vintage: 38 of the 142 tickers ended 2026-07-10 while 104 ran to 2026-07-31. Because the date axis was a UNION, the 38 short names read None for the final 15 sessions and were marked at ZERO - not a price. Every SEC number was affected (headline horizon effect overstated 3x: +5.84 pp published vs +1.87 pp actual); GATE reproduces exactly because it ends in 2013. Root cause fixed via an optional through= freshness contract in cache_fetch plus truncating the date axis to the earliest final bar and reporting mixed vintage loudly.
nodes.norm_label: mixed-vintage cache corruption (published sec numbers were wrong)

nodes.label: Extended re-run on a uniform longer window (NOT a second correction)
nodes.rationale: Labelled separately on purpose: the correction fixed WRONG numbers, this re-ran on MORE data after the whole universe was refreshed to a common through=2026-08-04 cutoff. GATE is byte-identical since it ends in 2013; SEC shifts only 0.2-0.6 pp (horizon +1.87 -> +2.06 pp, breadth -10.23 -> -9.60 pp). Why this matters more than the numbers: a conclusion that flipped on three extra weeks was never solid, and this one did not flip - that stability IS the result of the re-run. Both runs are kept side by side so they stay auditable.
nodes.norm_label: extended re-run on a uniform longer window (not a second correction)

nodes.label: The best cell in the factorial is still not a passing strategy
nodes.rationale: Cell 2 (12-1 momentum, top-3, 63-session hold) posts GATE CAGR 14.24% (< 15%) and DD 63.8% (> 60%) - failing BOTH D1 criteria, narrowly on return and clearly on drawdown, and still 13.33% at 15 bps. It also sits on a survivor universe where only a FAIL is clean, so its +28.5% SEC is uninterpretable as evidence of edge; and corr(cell 4, e6 rule) = +0.587 means these momentum cells would not solve the decorrelation problem either. The honest summary: we now know which wall we were hitting, and the wall behind it is drawdown.
nodes.norm_label: the best cell in the factorial is still not a passing strategy

nodes.label: X9 - pairs / relative-value (market-neutral family)
nodes.author: Evan Daruwalla
nodes.rationale: FAIL on 3 of 4 pre-registered criteria (attempt 37); only correlation passed at -0.057. H0 was the pre-declared favored prior and H0 won. Net GATE -2.50% / Sharpe -0.47 and SEC -6.71% / -1.40, ending at $294.16 from $1,000. Closes the last structurally different family the July-12 survey identified as in-scope and untested - the remaining candidates are 1-12 month horizons outside the swing scope, or data-gated.

nodes.label: The signal is smaller than the toll (not 'no signal')
nodes.rationale: A post-hoc zero-cost diagnostic splits the failure cleanly in two, and both modes are real and compound. First, the edge had ALREADY decayed before costs: gross Sharpe 0.43 in GATE (below the 0.50 bar even for free) and -0.05 in 2014+, literally nothing. Second, the cost structure then kills it: ~81 round trips/year at ~20 bps (4 legs) is ~16%/yr of drag, converting a nil gross edge into -70% of capital. The mechanism itself is NOT broken - 87.4% of trades converged, spreads do mean-revert - the reversion is simply smaller than four legs of transaction cost.
nodes.norm_label: the signal is smaller than the toll (not 'no signal')

nodes.label: Four-leg cost structure (5 bps per side per leg)
nodes.rationale: A round trip pays 4 legs = ~20 bps, deliberately NOT the 1 bp broad-ETF tier, because understating the leg count is the usual way this family gets flattered. Leveraged ETF members were also excluded since embedded decay breaks the mean-reverting premise.
nodes.norm_label: four-leg cost structure (5 bps per side per leg)

nodes.label: Decorrelation is not the scarce resource; edge is
nodes.rationale: Three consecutive decorrelation attempts - X8a GLD (+0.089), X8b TLT (-0.191), X9 pairs (-0.057) - all cleared the correlation bar comfortably and none cleared profitability. The three live sleeves therefore remain ~ONE strategy (m10 runs the identical e6 rule on 69.7% of 4,226 sessions; all three effectively long 65.3% of the time), and that is now a documented consequence of the evidence rather than an oversight.
nodes.norm_label: decorrelation is not the scarce resource; edge is

nodes.label: Undeployable at $1,000 even if it had cleared
nodes.rationale: Declared in prereg section 7 and restated despite being moot: Alpaca paper does not support fractional shorts and ~$167/leg cannot buy a whole share of most universe members. X9 tested the FAMILY, never a deployable configuration - the same wall X2b hit.
nodes.norm_label: undeployable at $1,000 even if it had cleared

nodes.label: Research Brief - TA swing trading executed by an AI agent (cold literature sweep)
nodes.author: Claude (Opus 5)
nodes.rationale: A COLD brief - project files deliberately unread by instruction - so it carries no verdict on this repo's work and is not a results doc. Desk research only, no backtests run; several numbers tagged UNVERIFIED inline. Its headline: the baseline as stated is half-right and the wrong half is the half most retail material emphasizes.
nodes.norm_label: research brief - ta swing trading executed by an ai agent (cold literature sweep)

nodes.label: Reconciliation against the project record (added 2026-08-06)
nodes.rationale: The brief's findings are NOT rewritten; the record wins where they conflict and this block records where that happens. Nothing in the brief is REFUTED - on every claim the repo has actually tested the two AGREE, reached independently: F1 chart patterns fail = M11 signal-dead; F4 costs bind = X9's 87.4% convergence yet -70% capital; F2 MA-timing overstated = six one-window deaths; F2 short-horizon reversal cost-bound = E1's overnight gap. What remains is one scope mismatch and one internal tension, not a correction of fact.

nodes.label: The crux - M12's 'horizon binds' is NOT the same claim as F2's long-horizon evidence
nodes.rationale: Same direction, different claims, for three reasons. (1) Different quantities: M12 held the signal constant and identified a COST/TURNOVER mechanism - the tell being that the horizon effect grows when cost triples - which is an argument about friction, while F2 is an argument about where the premium is documented. (2) M12 never reaches the literature's horizon: its winning cell is 63 sessions ~= 3 months while MOP-2012 and George/Hwang are 6-12 months, so its best cell is an extrapolation BELOW the evidence, not an arrival at it. (3) M12 cannot separate the explanations: moving only hold length makes 'longer = cheaper' and 'longer = more real signal' co-move.
nodes.norm_label: the crux - m12's 'horizon binds' is not the same claim as f2's long-horizon evidence

nodes.label: Internal tension - compressing the 52-week-high effect to K=3 / 5-20 days
nodes.rationale: Candidate #1 rests on George/Hwang - monthly-rebalanced, long-short, top/bottom 30%, 6-12 month holds - so recommending it AND compressing it reintroduces exactly the extrapolation F2 warns against. The brief calls the compression 'the untested part'; the record sharpens that: E3 already tested concentrated single-stock momentum and it FAILED. The compression is not merely untested - its nearest tested neighbour failed. The 52-week-high ANCHOR itself remains the one genuinely untested candidate, already flagged IN-SCOPE-UNTESTED by the 2026-07-12 method survey.
nodes.norm_label: internal tension - compressing the 52-week-high effect to k=3 / 5-20 days

nodes.label: F4 - cost arithmetic, not signal quality, is the binding constraint
nodes.rationale: Derivation, not a sourced claim: a K=1-3 book with 5-20 day holds implies ~25-100 round trips/year, so at 15 bps round-trip friction and 50 round trips the drag is ~7.5% of capital per year - comparable to the entire long-run equity risk premium. The cost model is therefore not a detail to add later; it determines whether a candidate is even ADMISSIBLE. The strategy must clear its own friction before it clears the benchmark, and the friction estimate must come from measured paper fills, not an assumed constant.
nodes.norm_label: f4 - cost arithmetic, not signal quality, is the binding constraint

nodes.label: fill_divergence exists but n=4 cannot calibrate a friction distribution
nodes.rationale: The measurement instrument F4 demands ALREADY EXISTS - fill_divergence, built 2026-07-28 in audit #2 - and holds 4 real sim-vs-broker fills: +0.0, +0.0, +1.3, -85.7 bps. It should be the data source rather than a new one. But 3 of the 4 are the same ticker (QQQ) on the same side, and the -85.7 bps outlier is a documented discipline break (an intraday fire), not spread. The harness can be SPECIFIED now; it cannot be CALIBRATED yet.
nodes.norm_label: fill_divergence exists but n=4 cannot calibrate a friction distribution

nodes.label: F8 - the validation harness is the actual deliverable
nodes.rationale: What separates this project from the 92 methodologically-compromised studies Park & Irwin surveyed is test discipline, not strategy. Minimum bar: Deflated Sharpe Ratio, Probability of Backtest Overfitting, and purged K-fold with embargo plus CPCV. The recommendation is to build the cost model and harness FIRST against a deliberately worthless signal, because that is the cheapest possible way to prove the harness actually rejects things - and it maps onto the existing frozen-regression discipline of pinning references, failing loud on drift, and never tuning a FAIL.
nodes.norm_label: f8 - the validation harness is the actual deliverable

nodes.label: F7 - an LLM agent is defensible only as a constrained veto overlay
nodes.rationale: On present evidence an LLM as primary decision-maker is a beta machine with a narrative generator attached: 0/19 studies reproducible, parametric look-ahead measurably inflates in-sample returns, and alpha vanishes under memory-controlled evaluation. The one defensible role is a veto or context overlay on top of a coded, independently-validated signal, evaluated strictly after the model's knowledge cutoff, with the coded signal alone as a mandatory control arm.
nodes.norm_label: f7 - an llm agent is defensible only as a constrained veto overlay

nodes.label: Ranked candidates for the signal layer (6 options)
nodes.rationale: Ranked by evidence quality x implementability at $100-1,000: (1) cross-sectional trend/52-week-high rank at K=3; (2) PEAD-timed entries - the only well-documented anomaly whose native horizon matches swing trading, but decayed and needing a point-in-time earnings feed the project lacks; (3) Osler-style support/resistance, best mechanism but FX order books and needs intraday data the EOD rule forbids; (4) image-CNN replication, strongest evidence but structurally incompatible; (5) LLM as decision-maker, highest narrative value and lowest evidentiary support; (6) classical chart patterns, weakest of the six and worth building only as a falsification exercise. Recommendation: neither #1 nor #5 first - the cost model and harness come first.

nodes.label: Signature defect: a guard that cannot fire
nodes.rationale: The project's single recurring defect class, counted to six variants: a threshold below the mathematical minimum of what it guards, a parameter no caller passes, a check needing two series in a single-series script, a raise caught by the function that raises it, a floor skipped on missing data, and (FJ) a guard that fires into a channel nobody reads.

nodes.label: Pre-registration before results
nodes.rationale: Every experiment's hypothesis, gates and predictions are committed to git BEFORE the runner exists, so a FAIL can never be tuned into a PASS. Risk appetite may change gate NUMBERS, never rigor.

nodes.label: Survivorship bias / only-a-FAIL-is-clean
nodes.rationale: The 39-name and 142-name stock universes contain only names that still trade, biasing results in the strategy's favour; therefore only a FAIL is interpretable evidence and a PASS is capped as UNINTERPRETABLE.

nodes.label: The structural null: no clean OOS high-return edge
nodes.rationale: Across 38 pre-registered attempts in six-plus families, zero clean out-of-sample high-return edges survived. The one PASS-HR (M10-1) is in-sample-composed on a survivor universe.

nodes.label: The 54-day record wedge
nodes.rationale: One malformed heading, '# Appendix BR-note', did not match the checker's appendix-letter pattern, so nextFreeLetter could not see it and append-record-entry.js refused EVERY append for 54 days. Resolved by demoting it to '## BR-note' rather than inventing a letter, because A..FJ has zero gaps and any legal letter would either duplicate BR or break the position-increases-with-letter invariant.

nodes.label: Table-of-Contents backfill (36 -> 166 entries)
nodes.rationale: Unwedging the record required satisfying the checker invariant TOC lines == appendix headings. 131 TOC lines were generated and appended after line 74; the generator was trusted only after reproducing 32 of 35 hand-written lines byte-identically, with the 3 differences display-text-only and anchors matching. Existing lines were left untouched: additive, not rewriting a prior hand.

nodes.label: Append-only record invariant
nodes.rationale: Prior appendices are never edited; corrections are written forward as new entries (e.g. a CORRECTION section inside a later appendix). Enforced by scripts/git-hooks/pre-commit delegating to the project-memory record checker.

nodes.label: Append-only guard bypass at commit 87db1c2
nodes.rationale: The pre-commit guard correctly refused the unwedging commit because it removed one previously committed line. Blast radius was MEASURED first (a staged-diff count of removed lines returned exactly 1) before committing with --no-verify on Evan's explicit one-off approval, with the reason in the commit message. The guard was not weakened, disabled or edited.

nodes.label: Per-sleeve missed-session detector
nodes.rationale: daily_swing_paper.py read SELECT DISTINCT date FROM paper_nav while paper_nav's PK is (sleeve, date), so a date counted as covered when ANY sleeve recorded it. The one real vanish it ever had to catch was the one kind it structurally could not see. Now a per-sleeve set difference over (sleeve, date) pairs, each sleeve's own first mark as its start.

nodes.label: ACKNOWLEDGED_NAV_HOLES as (sleeve, date) pairs
nodes.rationale: Converted from a bare date set to pairs, because a date-scoped acknowledgement would forgive a date for EVERY sleeve, re-introducing the cross-sleeve blindness in the acknowledgement path. Written as a literal, not derived from ps.SLEEVES, so a fourth sleeve never inherits a pre-acknowledged hole.

Backfilling was rejected because forward paper evidence that is reconstructed is not forward evidence. Standing consequence: 31 marks vs 36, so any cross-sleeve comparison must align on dates.

nodes.rationale: CLAUDE.md calls it mandatory in any universe filter because at $100-1,000 capital spread and slippage dominate. The call site tested adv is not None before comparing, so a data-starved name skipped the floor entirely; the function's own docstring instructed that behaviour, so both were changed together to fail closed on None.

nodes.label: F3 scope inversion
nodes.rationale: Measurement overturned the authorised premise: the 39-name survivor set breaches the floor 0 of 260,363 ticker-sessions, so re-running the eleven authorised stock experiments is pure compute for a guaranteed null, while 26 of the 29 frozen ETFs breach 16.07% of sessions. Wiring the floor into the immune backtests would ship the guard-that-cannot-fire defect a fifth time, deliberately.

nodes.label: STRESS_K = 4 dated exception
nodes.rationale: Resolved in CLAUDE.md as a documented exception rather than a code change: K=4 is the parameter the evidence actually covers (run_c1_residual_reversal.py and run_m10_1_nagel_switch.py both bottom-K=4). Dropping the live basket to K=3 would make the live sleeve implement a rule no backtest has run, which is the F2 defect class. Scope: the M10-1 stress branch only; e6_1x and e18_vixts stay K=1.

nodes.label: EOD-data-only rule
nodes.rationale: Signal at close, execute next open; no intraday logic until an intraday data source exists. Backed at runtime by the intraday-execution guard added after record DE.

nodes.label: Cold-audit program
nodes.rationale: Repeated exhaustive audits run by a fresh auditor with no inherited session belief. Audit #4's theme: the previous audit's fixes were DETECTIVE, not CORRECTIVE. Audit #3's theme: fixes applied at ONE site and claimed at ALL sites.

nodes.label: Landing-check practice
nodes.rationale: A fresh agent verifies claims against ARTIFACTS (diff, record entry, report) rather than session recollection. It has repeatedly refuted the project's own assertions: 8 asserted defects REFUTED in EO, the two-lost-sessions claim shown FALSE in EY, and 9 hyperedges shown destroyed in EU.
